proof:
Source. This is Step 2 of the parent proof (P. Mattila, Geometry of Sets and Measures in Euclidean Spaces, Lemma 15.13; M. G. Dall'Alba, The Besicovitch-Federer Projection Theorem, Padova 2020, Lemma 4.5), with the countable cover and the Lipschitz extension written out.

Notation. N := n + ℓ, ℝ^d := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), |·| the Euclidean norm, B(x, ρ) the open ball, Hⁿ := μHE[n]. P := W.starProjection is the orthogonal projection of ℝ^N onto W: P is linear, P(ℝ^N) = W, Pw = w for w ∈ W and |Pz| ≤ |z|. The hypothesis is
 (H) s|b − a| ≤ |P(b − a)| for all a, b ∈ E with |b − a| < r.

1. Countable cover by small pieces. ℝ^N is separable; fix an enumeration (d_k)_{k∈ℕ} of a countable dense subset (for instance the points with rational coordinates). Every x ∈ ℝ^N satisfies |x − d_k| < r/2 for some k. Put E_k := E ∩ B(d_k, r/2) for k ∈ ℕ. Then E = ⋃_k E_k, and |b − a| ≤ |b − d_k| + |d_k − a| < r for all a, b ∈ E_k.

2. P is injective on E_k with Lipschitz inverse. For a, b ∈ E_k, (H) and the linearity of P give s|b − a| ≤ |P(b − a)| = |Pb − Pa|. Hence Pa = Pb forces a = b, so P maps E_k bijectively onto P(E_k), and the inverse φ_k : P(E_k) → E_k, φ_k(Pa) := a, satisfies |φ_k(y) − φ_k(y′)| ≤ s⁻¹|y − y′| for all y, y′ ∈ P(E_k) (apply the inequality to a := φ_k(y), b := φ_k(y′)).

3. Lipschitz extension of φ_k to all of ℝ^N. If E_k = ∅ put G_k := 0. Otherwise, for each coordinate i ∈ {1, …, N} the real function φ_k^{(i)} := ⟨φ_k(·), e_i⟩ is s⁻¹-Lipschitz on the set P(E_k) ⊆ ℝ^N; by McShane's extension (Simon Ch. 2, 1.2; Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real), e.g. g^{(i)}(y) := inf_{z ∈ P(E_k)} (φ_k^{(i)}(z) + s⁻¹|y − z|), there is an s⁻¹-Lipschitz g^{(i)} : ℝ^N → ℝ with g^{(i)} = φ_k^{(i)} on P(E_k). Put G_k(y) := Σ_i g^{(i)}(y) e_i. Then |G_k(y) − G_k(y′)| = (Σ_i |g^{(i)}(y) − g^{(i)}(y′)|²)^{1/2} ≤ √N s⁻¹ |y − y′|, so G_k : ℝ^N → ℝ^N is Lipschitz and G_k = φ_k on P(E_k). (Equivalently one may use Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_pi for the sup norm on Fin N → ℝ and transport it through the continuous linear equivalence with EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N); only some finite Lipschitz constant is needed.)

4. Parametrizing W by ℝⁿ. Since finrank W = n = finrank ℝⁿ, there is a linear isometric equivalence ι : ℝⁿ ≃ W (send an orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ to an orthonormal basis of W); J := (inclusion W → ℝ^N) ∘ ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N is a linear isometry with J(ℝⁿ) = W. Put F_k := G_k ∘ J : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N; since J is 1-Lipschitz, F_k is Lipschitz (constant √N/s).

5. E_k ⊆ F_k(ℝⁿ). Let a ∈ E_k. Then Pa ∈ W = J(ℝⁿ), say Pa = J(u) with u ∈ ℝⁿ, and F_k(u) = G_k(Pa) = φ_k(Pa) = a.

6. Conclusion. E = ⋃_k E_k ⊆ ⋃_k F_k(ℝⁿ). Taking M₀ := ∅ (Hⁿ(∅) = 0) and the Lipschitz maps F_k (k ∈ ℕ) verifies the definition of CountablyRectifiable n E: μHE[n] M₀ = 0, every F_k is LipschitzWith some constant, and E ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_k range F_k. ∎
key_steps: Cover E by the countably many pieces E_k := E ∩ B(d_k, r/2), (d_k) dense; points of one piece are at distance < r.
On each piece s|b − a| ≤ |Pb − Pa|, so P is injective there with an s⁻¹-Lipschitz inverse φ_k on P(E_k).
Extend φ_k coordinatewise (McShane / LipschitzOnWith.extend_real) to a Lipschitz map G_k : ℝ^N → ℝ^N.
Precompose with a linear isometry J : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N onto W; F_k := G_k ∘ J is Lipschitz and E_k ⊆ F_k(ℝⁿ).
E ⊆ ⋃_k F_k(ℝⁿ) with M₀ := ∅, i.e. CountablyRectifiable n E.
